bull.b: Strong operating and free cash flow provides funding for sustaining investment, growth projects and shareholder returns. Its quality is supported by TTM free cash flow of about $12.8B, roughly in line with net income.

Net cash and low leverage improve resilience through commodity cycles and give Newmont flexibility to fund projects, absorb operating disruptions and maintain capital returns without relying heavily on new borrowing.

Resolving the Nevada Gold Mines dispute removes a material governance overhang and clarifies asset, liability and approval frameworks. Better alignment between partners should support more consistent decision-making and long-term portfolio execution.

bear.b: Lower revenue and declining volumes indicate that earnings remain exposed to mine sequencing, grades, recoveries and commodity prices. This makes sustained growth less predictable even after the recent profitability rebound.

bear.t: Cost inflation and project execution risk
bear.b: Mining inflation and operational disruptions can reduce margins and defer production benefits. Cadia support and approval requirements, alongside higher sustaining and project costs, create continuing execution risk across the investment pipeline.

Exposure to changing fiscal terms and stakeholder requirements can raise costs, delay approvals or constrain mine plans. Ghana illustrates the broader risk that regulatory and geopolitical developments may affect asset economics over time.
